**1. Facility & Operations Management**

* Lead daily facility operations, ensuring efficiency, productivity, and effective resource allocation.
* Oversee engineering, production, quality, procurement, logistics, and administration.
* Establish operational targets, manage facility utilization, and drive continuous improvement.

**2. Engine Maintenance & Production**

* Oversee CFM56-3, CFM56-5B, and CFM56-7B maintenance activities, including shop visits, performance restoration, troubleshooting, and module repairs.
* Manage engine induction, inspection, repair, assembly, testing, and release processes.
* Monitor turnaround times (TAT), production schedules, material availability, and maintenance quality.
* Ensure maintenance is performed in accordance with approved technical data and manufacturer requirements.

**3. Quality & Regulatory Compliance**

* Ensure compliance with applicable GCAA, EASA, FAA, and other relevant aviation regulations.
* Maintain maintenance organization approvals, quality systems, technical records, and component traceability.
* Oversee audits, corrective actions, safety standards, and regulatory compliance.

**4. Financial & Commercial Management**

* Take responsibility for facility revenue, profitability, budgets, and financial performance.
* Control labor, material, subcontracting, and operational costs.
* Review commercial quotations, maintenance work scopes, and additional findings to optimize margins.
* Monitor financial forecasts, commercial risks, and customer payment performance.

**5. Business Development & Customer Relations**

* Develop business opportunities with airlines, aircraft operators, lessors, engine owners, and MRO organizations.
* Secure CFM56 engine maintenance contracts and long-term service agreements.
* Lead customer negotiations, maintain strategic partnerships, and ensure customer satisfaction.
* Identify cross-selling opportunities across DTX Aerospace business units.

**6. Leadership & Workforce Management**

* Lead multidisciplinary teams of engineers, technicians, inspectors, and administrative personnel.
* Oversee workforce planning, recruitment, training, performance management, and succession planning.
* Promote accountability, teamwork, technical excellence, and a strong safety culture.

**7. Supply Chain & Strategic Development**

* Oversee procurement, inventory, tooling, equipment, and supplier relationships.
* Ensure timely availability of materials and maintenance resources.
* Develop business growth strategies, expand maintenance capabilities, and identify operational improvement opportunities.
* Report operational, financial, and commercial performance to senior management.

Qualifications & Experience

* Bachelor's degree in Aeronautical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Aviation Management, or a related field preferred.
* **Minimum 10 years of experience**
  in commercial aircraft engine maintenance, MRO, or aviation technical services.
* **Minimum 5 years in senior management**
  , facility management, or operational leadership.
* Proven experience managing commercial jet engine maintenance facilities or engine repair operations.
* Strong technical knowledge of
  **CFM56-3, CFM56-5B, and/or CFM56-7B**
  engines.
* Hands-on understanding of engine shop visits, performance restoration, troubleshooting, module maintenance, and repair processes.
* Strong financial management, budgeting, cost control, and commercial negotiation skills.
* Experience managing production performance, turnaround times, regulatory compliance, and technical teams.
* Established industry relationships and business development experience.
* Previous experience within the
  **Middle East aviation industry**
  is highly advantageous.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

* **Financial:**
  Revenue growth, profitability, cost control, and margin improvement.
* **Operational:**
  Engine turnaround time, on-time delivery, productivity, and facility utilization.

  Regulatory compliance, audit performance, first-pass quality, and reduced rework.

  New customer acquisition, contract conversion, recurring business, and customer retention.

* Strong leadership, strategic thinking, and decision-making.
* Hands-on technical and operational management approach.
* Commercial awareness and financial discipline.
* Excellent communication, negotiation, and stakeholder management.
* Ability to lead multicultural teams and manage competing priorities.
* High standards of integrity, accountability, safety, and professionalism.

The position is based in the Middle East and requires regional and international travel for customer meetings, supplier engagements, regulatory discussions, and business development activities.

Title: Vice President, Operations & Client Delivery
Description:

Physicians Revenue Group, Inc. and its family of commonly held companies serve physician and dental

practices across the United States. Our business units provide medical billing and revenue cycle

management, dental revenue cycle management, value-based care programs, digital marketing agency

services, healthcare cybersecurity, and healthcare technology, supported by teams in the United States

and abroad.

**About the role**

This role leads service delivery and client success across our family of companies, which provide revenue

cycle management, dental revenue cycle, and value-based care services to physician and dental

practices nationwide, delivered by onshore and offshore teams.

You will bring delivery and client success together under one standard: every client gets consistent

service, every leader runs to a scorecard, and every team knows what good looks like. This role is for a

healthcare operator who has led directors, held them accountable, and grown client retention at scale.

**Core responsibilities**

**I. Enterprise operations leadership**

* Lead the directors responsible for revenue cycle, dental, and value-based care operations, and the  offshore delivery leadership supporting them.
* Set one operating standard across business units: decision rights, escalation paths, scorecards, and review cadence.
* Coach, develop, and hold directors accountable; address underperformance promptly and fairly.

**II. Client delivery and retention**

* Own client retention and satisfaction outcomes across business units.
* Ensure account transitions, manager changes, and onboarding happen without service disruption.
* Run quarterly client performance reviews on verified data.

**III. Offshore and hybrid delivery**

* Align onshore client success with offshore delivery teams on staffing, quality, productivity, and escalation.
* Set service levels and quality standards that apply equally to onshore and offshore teams.

**IV. Quality, compliance, and controls**

* Partner with the compliance function so delivery meets payer and regulatory requirements, and act on audit findings promptly.
* Ensure documented SOPs, version control, and training are in place for every service line.

**V. Commercial partnership**

* Work alongside the commercial teams as the operational and technical leader, joining client presentations and high-level client discussions where needed.
* Partner with sales and business development on scoping, pricing inputs, and implementation readiness.

**VI. Growth and new service lines**

* Build delivery models for new DSO and MSO services and support new client implementations.

**VII. Financial performance**

* Own delivery cost, margin, and productivity targets for each business unit.
* Use operating data to set staffing plans and improve unit economics.

**90-day priorities**

* **Day 1-30:**
  Meet directors, key clients, and offshore leadership. Review scorecards, retention data, and open issues.
* **Day 31-60:**
  Implement one operating cadence and director scorecards across business units. Address the highest-risk client accounts.
* **Day 61-90:**
  Deliver a 12-month operations plan covering retention, quality, offshore alignment, margin, and new service line readiness.

**12-month success metrics**

* Client retention at or above target in every business unit.
* Every director on a scorecard, reviewed monthly, with clear actions on underperformance.
* Delivery margin and productivity targets met.
* Audit findings closed on time with verification.
* Delivery model in place for new DSO and MSO services.

**Qualifications**

**Required**

* 12+ years in healthcare operations, including at least 5 years leading directors or multi-site
* operations.
* Operations and client delivery experience in a services organization.
* Revenue cycle management experience in a services or outsourcing organization.
* Experience leading offshore or hybrid delivery teams.
* Track record of improving client retention and operating margin.
* Bachelor’s degree.

**Preferred**

* Client success leadership experience, especially in healthcare. Highly preferred, though strong,
* transferable operations and client delivery experience will also be considered.
* Value-based care, care management, or dental revenue cycle experience.
* Experience with DSO or MSO operations.
* MBA or MHA.

**Performance framework**

* Quarterly review against retention, quality and compliance, margin, and leadership development.
* Bonus tied to quality, retention, and margin KPIs, not to billing volume.

**Career growth path**

This role is the senior operating leader for service delivery and is positioned for expanded executive

responsibility as the organization scales.

As part of our leadership team, this role may support initiatives across other business units as the

organization grows.

**Job Information**

Time Type: Full time, non-exempt

Location: On-site (Downers Grove, IL)

Compensation: $165,000 - 185,000 + up to 15% annual bonus

Benefits: Health insurance, 401(k) with employer match, paid time off, and professional

development support.

The NS&S Team is seeking an experienced and motivated individual to join our high performing team as an Operations Manager.

Key responsibilities include identifying, analyzing, and resolving complex problems, ensuring compliance with policies, and developing and implementing new processes to improve operating efficiency and ensure accuracy of workflow. * Develops and analyzes procedures to enhance unit and/or product-related activities and oversees budget and expense management, reporting, and forecasting for designated areas
* Evaluates efficiencies and identifies areas of improvement and growth to the overall process, identifying data, metrics, and key performance indicators to measure process effectiveness
* Aligns bank priorities and strategies to employee metrics and goals and strives to recognize, encourage, and improve team performance to support an inclusive work environment

* Maintains a full understanding of the team's performance. Understanding the performance of each person, using long- and short-term analysis of key performance indicators, observations, and anecdotal information
* Identifies positive and negative patterns driving the performance
* Coaches the team and individuals to sustain positive patterns and mitigate negative patterns to improve or sustain performance
* Sustains a process excellence culture to maintain consistent and iterative improvements in all aspects of the operation and employee experience
* Actively participates in routines and practices to accurately assess key performance indicators and executes on actions needed to improve and maintain the health of the operation and the employee experience
* Executes long and short-term strategic plans to drive improvements in client care, efficiency, employee engagement and growth
* Makes sound judgements based on data to balance risks with rewards, maintain control discipline, and respond to change
* Engages in ongoing personal education to maintain a current working knowledge of the market, technology that would benefit the operation, best practices in employee engagement, and updated skill set

* Opportunity & Inclusion Champion: Creates an inclusive team where members are treated fairly and respectfully.
* Manager of Process & Data: Demonstrates and expects process knowledge, data driven decisions, simplicity and continuous improvement.
* Enterprise Advocate & Communicator: Delivers clear and concise messages that motivate, convey the “why" and connects contributions to business results.
* Risk Manager: Leads and encourages the identification, escalation and resolution of potential risks.
* People Manager & Coach: Knows and develops team members through coaching and feedback.
* Financial Steward: Manages expenses and demonstrates an owner's mindset.
* Enterprise Talent Leader: Recruits, on-boards and develops talent, and supports talent mobility for career growth.
* Driver of Business Outcomes: Delivers results through effective team management, structure, and routines.

**Required Qualifications:**

* 1+ years of experience as Manager, Assistant Manager or Proficiency Coach in a contact center or relevant work experience.
* Advanced/Expert MS Office skills, especially Excel and PowerPoint

**About Us:**

Marquette Transportation Company and Canal Barge Company are leaders in the marine transportation industry. Following investments by Redwood Holdings in Marquette and Canal Barge, the family of brands now includes Marquette River and Offshore divisions, Traust Marine Transportation, Canal Barge Company, Illinois Marine Towing, Canal Terminal Company, Canal Analytical and Environmental Services and Pelican Marine. This integrated network builds one of the industry's largest fleets with nearly 150 vessels, more than 4,000 barges, over 100 deck barges and 2,000 skilled mariners.

  

Headquartered in Paducah, Kentucky, and founded in 1978, Marquette is a leading provider of marine transportation services. Through an integrated towing network, Marquette operates across more than 6,000 miles of navigable waterways, including the Mississippi River System and its tributaries, the Gulf Intracoastal Waterway and the nearshore tugboat market.

  

Founded in 1933 and headquartered in New Orleans, Louisiana, Canal Barge is one of the largest privately-owned marine transportation companies in the United States. Canal Barge has a successful track record of developing long-term and mutually profitable partnerships with major companies in the refining, petrochemical, power generation, oilfield service, construction, and materials industries.

**Position Summary**

The Operations Manager – Tanking has accountability for the company's vessel tankerman workforce and its cargo transfer performance. The role hires, develops and manages tankermen, drives safety and incident-free transfers, and is integral to incident response if something goes wrong.

**Initial focus:** lead the alignment of vessel tanking operations under one unified standard: one set of procedures, training, equipment expectations and performance measures across every Traust vessel.

Safety and reliability is what our customers expect. This role makes sure the tankerman team delivers it every day: barges prepared ahead of the dock call, transfers that run clean and on time, and a safety record customers can count on.

We are looking for a steady, visible leader in the Houston area, someone that will develop trust and respect with customers, mariners and peers.

  

**Principal Responsibilities**

***Unified tanking standard (initial priority)***

* Assess current tanking practices, procedures and equipment across all Traust vessels.
* Define one unified standard for cargo transfers: procedures, checklists, PPE, equipment and documentation.
* Roll out the standard through training, field verification and clear accountability for tankermen.
* Align the standard with TSG, Port Captains, Compliance, Logistics and Sales so customers see one consistent operation.
* Measure adoption and close gaps to ensure the standard is how every transfer is done.

***Shore tanking partnership (TSG)***

* Exchange best practices and lessons learned across the Traust fleet.
* Align on PPE standards, organizational policy and core tanking expectations so the company presents one consistent approach to customers and regulators.
* Coordinate on shared topics such as regulatory changes, hose and equipment practices, and customer and terminal requirements.
* Explore career paths between vessel and shore tanking to develop and retain talent.

***Hiring and onboarding***

* Own the full hiring cycle for vessel tankermen: workforce planning, sourcing, interviewing and selection.
* Build and run a structured onboarding program covering company procedures, vessel familiarization and transfer standards.
* Own Verification of Tankerman-PIC credentials, MMC endorsements, TWIC and drug-testing compliance before assignment.
* Partner with Training to assess competency and develop tankermen toward higher endorsements and leadership roles.

***Placement and deployment***

* Place tankermen across the fleet based on skills, endorsements, cargo experience and vessel needs.
* Work alongside Port Captains and Logistics to match tankerman coverage to barge movements and customer schedules.
* Work with the Crewing department to manage rotations, relief coverage and staffing gaps.

***Barge make ready***

* Partner with vessel crews, tankermen and Port Captains to drive a strong make-ready culture across the fleet.
* Hold the line on company make-ready inspections: thorough, complete and documented every time.
* Surface deficiencies early and work with Barge Maintenance to prioritize, schedule and close out repairs with enough lead time that dock calls are never at risk.
* Coordinate with Logistics and terminals so barge readiness lines up with scheduled dock windows.
* Use make-ready findings and trends to target training, equipment fixes and procedure updates.

***Safety, compliance and proactive mitigation***

* Set and enforce cargo transfer standards in line with 33 CFR 155/156, 46 CFR, company SMS and customer requirements.
* Identify risk before it becomes an incident: transfer audits, ride-alongs, near-miss trends and equipment condition (hoses, gaskets, connections).
* Lead pre-job planning and hazard reviews for higher-risk or unfamiliar cargoes.
* Keep the team audit-ready for USCG, customer vetting and terminal inspections.

***Incident response***

* Serve as the operational lead for tankerman-related incidents, spills and near misses.
* Coordinate immediate response with Port Captains, HSE, the QI/response contractors and customers.
* Lead or support root cause investigations and close out corrective actions.

***Continuous improvement***

* Track and report transfer performance: incidents, delays, overtime, turnover and customer feedback.
* Standardize procedures, checklists and best practices across the tankerman group.
* Bring field feedback into equipment, procedure and training decisions.
  

**Key Working Relationships**

  

**Port Captains (including Unit Tow)**

Day-to-day partner on tankerman placement, vessel readiness and problem solving; aligns tankerman coverage and transfer standards with unit tow operations

  

**Logistics, Unit Tow Sales and Allocations**

Aligns tankerman deployment and barge readiness with allocations, barge movements, loading windows and customer commitments; supports vetting and new liquid business with a clear view of tankerman capacity

  

**HSE and Training**

Builds compliance, competency and incident investigation into how the team works

  

**Crewing / HR**

Supports recruiting pipeline, pay practices and employee engagement

  

**TSG (shore tanking)**

Align on the company's view of tanking: best practices, PPE, training methodologies, policy and career paths

**Leadership Attributes**

* **Leads beyond the org chart:** builds trust and gets results with Port Captains, Logistics and Sales, not just direct reports.
* **Sees the whole operation:** connects tanking to vessel operations, scheduling, customer commitments and efficiency / expense management.
* **Builds leaders:** coaches, develops and grows a bench of strong vessel, field, and shoreside talent. Thoughtful in team design and building team capabilities.
* **Business-minded:** understands how operational decisions drive customer satisfaction, revenue and costs.
* **Steady under pressure:** a calm, credible presence in the field, during an incident and in the leadership room.
* **Holds the standard:** consistent, fair and visible in the field.
* **Communicates up and out:** gives senior leadership clear, honest updates and recommendations.
* **Ready for more:** takes ownership of broader scope as Houston operations grow.
  

**Qualifications**

***Required***

* 7+ years in inland marine liquid cargo operations, including hands-on tankerman experience.
* 3+ years successfully leading people, in the field or shoreside.
* Working knowledge of 33 CFR 155/156, 46 CFR Subchapters D and O, and liquid cargo transfer practices.
* Track record in hiring, developing and holding crews accountable.
* Calm, decisive incident response experience.
* Strong communicator with mariners, customers and senior leaders.
* Lives in or will relocate to the Houston area; able to respond to the field and travel as needed.
* Valid TWIC.

***Preferred***

* Current or prior Tankerman-PIC (Barge) endorsement.
* Experience on the Houston Ship Channel and Gulf Intracoastal Waterway.
* Familiarity with customer vetting and terminal requirements (e.g., ACV/OCIMF-style inspections).
* Experience with Subchapter M, TSMS or ISM-based safety systems.
* Port Captain, Port Engineer or comparable shoreside operations experience.
  

**Measures of Success**

* One tanking standard adopted and verified across all vessels.
* Zero preventable spills and fewer transfer-related incidents and near misses.
* **Builds tankering capability through effective recruiting, retention and effective competency training.**
* Barges consistently prepared ahead of dock calls, with transfers on schedule and fewer tankerman-related delays.
* Clean USCG, customer and terminal audit results.
* Port Captains, Logistics and Sales see this role as a reliable partner.
  

**Working Conditions**

* Office-based in Houston with regular time on docks, fleets, barges and towboats.
* On call for incident response, including nights, weekends and holidays.
* Work in marine and industrial settings: weather exposure, climbing, uneven and wet surfaces, and required PPE.
